class: A failing step does not stop the step after it: a gate piped into a filter (`gate | tail`) takes the filter's exit status, and a command on its own line (or after `;`) runs whatever the line before returned - so a following commit, push or merge goes ahead after a failed gate; chaining with && is not enough when the gate's output is piped.
mechanism: The W-024 round-10 builder ran the CI mirror piped to tail and chained the push with &&; tail exited 0, the pricing-scan failure did not stop the push, and a red branch reached origin.

first_seen.evidence: builder report: ci_local 12 passed, 2 failed (tests/engine/test_pricing_scan.py) yet `git push` ran in the same && chain after `| tail`

fix: Run a gate as its own command (no pipe), or with `set -o pipefail`, and read its summary from the log file it writes; briefs state this rule.

checks: scripts/hooks/gate_before_commit.py (project PreToolUse hook on Bash|PowerShell, wired in .claude/project/hooks.json): refuses git commit / git push / merge_when_green after an earlier step that is piped, or joined by ;, a newline or ||, unless set -e / ErrorActionPreference Stop and no earlier step is piped
tests/hooks/test_gate_before_commit.py (the brief's allow/refuse table, fail-open, stdin round trip)
detection.note: Issue #155. Fails open on any parse error. Covers commands run through the Bash and PowerShell tools only; a script file that does the same inside itself is not seen. PARTIAL: merged by owner choice 2026-10-10 (owner question 6) with known bypasses open in #191 - `$(...)`/backticks on a setup line, a PowerShell assignment that runs a command, `set -e` with `&&`/`!`, and wrappers such as xargs, timeout, eval, cmd /c.

occurrences.evidence: red branch pushed past a piped gate

a resolution script stopped on its own assert, but `git add && git commit` on the next line still ran and committed conflict markers into the merge commit; caught before push and amended (agit grep for markers on HEAD: no match after the amend)
